q1_issues.issue: The universal "each age has left its mark" is buried inside the sealed Theme term as a bare (Implication ...) conjunct together with (QuantifierPhrase age leave "each"), so neither carries the STV the instruction set requires ((STV 1.0 0.9) for the distributing rule, (STV 1.0 0.99) for the companion) and the quantifier's force is lost.

q2_gaps: sealing a QUANTIFIED clause under a propositional attitude — the sealing rule describes only ground atoms nested as one term ((And ...)), and gives no way for an (Implication ...) or a (QuantifierPhrase ...) companion inside a seal to carry its own strength/confidence

impersonal / generic pronoun subject "one" ("one feels that ...") — the pronoun rule covers he/she/it/they only, so it is unclear whether this is a single existential person witness or a generic over person

factivity of "feel that P": "feel" is listed among the PERCEPTION verbs, whose finite that-clause the instruction set routes to the FACTIVE attitude (seal + assert), yet "feel" appears in neither the factive nor the non-factive attitude list and "feels that" is not factive in English
notes: Event structure, roles (Experiencer/Patient/Agent), Manner "slowly", present-perfect to (Past e), the (sk_mark $x) dependent Skolem and the definite-referent projection of (Member sk_city_1 city) all follow the instruction set. The only substantive problem is that the second sealed conjunct is a rule, a shape the sealing construct cannot carry.
